Chosen for DISTINCT SILHOUETTES above all — a row of generic four-legged
chairs tells an audience nothing about the dataset's variety.
TWO LISTS, and they are not the same list. `names` is the RENDER SET: which
objects slide_renders.py rasterizes to gallery_NN.png, in slot order. Slide 5
shows `slide_row`, a chosen subset, and the slide resolves each entry to a
tile BY OBJECT NAME through the render manifest — never by slot index. That
seam is deliberate: slot numbering shifts whenever the render set changes,
and a slide addressing tiles by number silently shows different chairs when
it does.
The composition is NOT a free choice: 3 of the 6 in slide_row sit below
chroma 0.05, against 51.3% of the training split. The row therefore matches
the dataset's achromatic fraction to within a percent, which matters because
the chroma histogram beside it on the slide makes exactly that claim. A
prettier row with five colourful chairs would have contradicted its own
figure. s05_data.py recomputes both numbers from chair_colour_stats.csv at
build time rather than reading them from here, so the caption cannot drift
away from the row it sits under.

The moulded shell was added to make six. Two reasons, both structural: it
carries the only thin-wire base in the row (the other five all stand on
solid or tubular legs), and it is achromatic, which takes the row from 2
grey of 5 to 3 of 6 — 50% against the split's 51.3%. At five the row
undersold how grey this dataset is by eleven points, directly under a
histogram whose whole point is that number.
